title: Certificates of Deposit: The Renewal Principal Read From the Ledger at Booking
content:
When a certificate among Piedmont Crescent Bank's Certificates of Deposit renews, the Jumbo Bonus of its new term turns on how large the certificate is. That size, called here the Renewal Principal, is not copied from the balance field on the certificate. It is read from the certificate's own ledger.

## Definition

The Renewal Principal is a reading of the ledger taken at the moment the renewal is booked. Counted in: every deposit entry, every interest credit that compounding placed into the certificate, and every penalty reversal entry. Counted out: every withdrawal entry and every penalty entry. Interest sent away to a checking or savings account under a payout choice is ignored altogether, because it never formed part of the certificate's capital.

Even though the renewed term counts its days from the old maturity date, the reading belongs to the moment of booking. Whatever stands on the ledger at that moment is therefore part of it, including money added or taken out during grace and any penalty reversal entry.

Should the balance field on the certificate disagree with this reading, the reading prevails.

## Points of judgement

**May the Renewal Principal be net of a penalty the certificate terms do not allow?** No. A charge that the terms oblige the bank to give back is not one the certificate is meant to bear, and the new term is priced on a Renewal Principal free of every such charge. The figure being a ledger reading, a charge of that kind has been lifted from it only where its reversal entry is on the ledger.

**Is the Renewal Principal the balance as it stood on the maturity date?** No. The term's dates run from the maturity date, but the size is read from the ledger at booking.

**Interest for the term's final months went to the owner's checking account. Does it count?** No. Paid-out interest plays no part in the reading.

## Worked reading (hypothetical ledger at the moment of booking)

Deposit entries total USD 88000.00; compounding has added USD 4150.00; USD 600.00 of interest went out to a savings account; one withdrawal entry of USD 1500.00 and one penalty entry of USD 45.00 appear; there is no reversal entry. The Renewal Principal is 88000.00 plus 4150.00, less 1500.00, less 45.00: USD 90605.00, the USD 600.00 of paid-out interest playing no part. Suppose that USD 45.00 penalty is one the terms require to be given back: with its reversal entry on the ledger the reading is USD 90650.00, while a ledger without that entry still shows the charge.
